area: middleware: scope (all paths, all hosts, all methods it inspects)
current_behavior: middleware.ts has no `export const config`, so Vercel runs it for every route in the project (Vercel docs: 'Routing Middleware will be invoked for every route in your project', default runtime nodejs). It never inspects the Host header (only url.origin for Markdown bodies). shouldNegotiate() returns true for GET/HEAD on every path except /_astro/, /favicons/, /images/, /scripts/ prefixes and a fixed extension list (js css png jpg jpeg gif webp svg ico pdf xml txt woff woff2 map webmanifest json); any *.md path always negotiates. vercel.json host redirect runs BEFORE middleware (verified live: `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://jsolly.com/about/` returns 308 to www, not Markdown).
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: (1) Every /blog/* and /recipes/* request invokes the function (cost + latency), incl. images. (2) If blogthedata.com were attached to the jsolly-website Vercel project, middleware would run for it too and any blogthedata.com path NOT matched by an explicit host-scoped redirect would fall through to jsolly.com content (duplicate content on the old domain; Markdown bodies would advertise the blogthedata origin). Separate redirect-only project avoids this.
proposed_resolution: Export `config.matcher` that excludes /_astro, /media, /recipes-pwa, /favicons, /images, /data, *.xml/rss/atom feeds, or invert to an allowlist of agent-negotiated routes. Keep blogthedata.com on its own redirect-only Vercel project (no middleware). If domains are ever attached to this project, add an explicit final host-scoped catch-all redirect and a host guard in middleware.
evidence: vercel.com/docs/routing-middleware/api ('every route in your project'); live curl 2026-10-04 apex /about/ with Accept: text/markdown -> HTTP/2 308 location https://www.jsolly.com/about/ with no vary header; middleware.ts:9-20

area: middleware: Markdown negotiation 404s every real blog/recipe page
current_behavior: agentResponse(): path ending .md -> always Markdown (200 if key in PAGES else 404 'Not found' Markdown). Otherwise, if shouldNegotiate: preferredType(Accept); null -> 406 text/plain; 'text/markdown' -> Markdown 200 for the 5 PAGES keys (/, /about, /contact, /privacy, /terms) else 404 Markdown; 'text/html' -> pass through to static HTML. Paths NOT in agent-pages pass through only when Accept resolves to text/html (including */* or no Accept). No matcher limits it. Production confirms: GET /blog/foo/ with Accept: text/markdown -> 404 text/markdown; GET /blog/foo.md -> 404 markdown; /blog/x.avif with Accept: application/json -> 406.
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: Any /blog/<slug>/ or /recipes/... request with Accept: text/markdown gets a 404 even though the page exists; this holds for every layout choice because middleware sees every path (live: GET /blog/foo/ with Accept: text/markdown -> 404 text/markdown). CONDITIONAL on layout choice: if blog pages adopt DST's Layout.astro head, lines 38-40 emit <link rel=alternate type=text/markdown href=...slug.md> for every non-noindex page, advertising .md siblings that 404; in the overlay the posts render through the blog's Base.astro, which emits no such link. public/llms.txt:5 also claims HTML pages honor Accept: text/markdown and that an unknown path returns HTTP 404 with a Markdown recovery body.
proposed_resolution: Recommended shape: discriminate by ROUTE EXISTENCE, not by URL prefix. Generate a build-time manifest of real pages (blog posts, index, recipes) and have middleware consult it: known route + Accept text/markdown -> Markdown (phase 2: from generated static Markdown siblings, one source of truth for both the manifest and the bodies); unknown route -> keep the existing contract (404 Markdown recovery body, as llms.txt promises). A prefix rule that passes /blog/ and /recipes/ through on a miss would instead return an HTML 404 for /blog/nonexistent/ with Accept: text/markdown and break that promise. Phase 1 until the manifest exists: do not advertise a Markdown alternate on blog/recipe pages (only relevant if they use Layout.astro) and keep the 404 Markdown behavior. Update agent-pages.ts (notFoundMarkdown links; home/about/contact blog links), llms.txt and accept-negotiate.test.ts accordingly.
evidence: Probe run in scratch clone (node --experimental-strip-types) of agentResponse(): /blog/some-post/ accept=text/markdown -> 404 text/markdown; /recipes/meals/ accept=text/markdown -> 404; /blog/some-post.md -> 404; live curl https://www.jsolly.com/blog/foo/ Accept text/markdown -> HTTP 404 content-type text/markdown vary Accept

area: middleware: RSS/Atom feeds receive 406 for typical feed-reader Accept headers
current_behavior: Feed URLs are extensionless (blog emits /rss and /atom as extensionless files). shouldNegotiate('/blog/rss/') = true, so preferredType(Accept) runs; if Accept lists only application/rss+xml / application/atom+xml (no */*), neither text/html nor text/markdown matches -> notAcceptable() 406.
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: Feed readers sending `Accept: application/rss+xml` (or a list without */*) get HTTP 406 at jsolly.com/blog/rss/ and /blog/atom/. Probe: GET /blog/rss/ accept=application/rss+xml -> 406 text/plain; same for atom. Also any unlisted extension (.avif .mp4 .ipynb .zip .html .mjs .wasm) with a non-matching Accept returns 406 (live: /blog/x.avif + Accept application/json -> 406).
proposed_resolution: Invert the logic: negotiate only for paths that are HTML pages (known agent-page keys, or an explicit allowlist /blog/ and /blog/<slug>/ and /recipes/...), and always pass through feeds (/blog/rss*, /blog/atom*), /media/, /data/, /recipes-pwa/, service-worker files. Add unit tests for feed Accept headers. Replace the extension denylist with an allowlist.
evidence: mw-probe run in scratch clone: `GET /blog/rss/ accept=application/rss+xml -> shouldNegotiate=true agentResponse=406 text/plain`; `/blog/atom/ ... 406`; `/media/x.avif accept=image/avif -> 406`; live curl /blog/x.avif Accept application/json -> HTTP/2 406

area: middleware: .md files in public/ are hijacked (assistant data)
current_behavior: Any pathname ending .md is answered by agentResponse before static files are consulted: PAGES lookup, else 404 Markdown.
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: The recipe assistant data file public/data/recipe-library.md (served at /data/recipe-library.md, also precached by the recipe service worker and generated by scripts/recipes/sync-assistant-data.mjs) would return a Markdown 404 instead of the file. Probe: GET /data/recipe-library.md -> 404 text/markdown (also with Accept: application/json). The sibling /data/recipe-library.json passes (json is in STATIC_EXT_RE). By inference (not exercised in production), the recipe SW's cache.addAll would then reject on this URL and abort SW install.
proposed_resolution: Exempt real static prefixes (/data/, /media/, /recipes/ data downloads) from the .md branch, or restrict the .md branch to keys that exist in PAGES / the generated blog Markdown manifest and otherwise pass through. If the assistant data moves under /recipes/ (e.g. /recipes/data/recipe-library.md), the exemption must be updated and pwa-build's URL list and the sync scripts' output paths changed together.
evidence: mw-probe: `GET /data/recipe-library.md accept=(none) -> shouldNegotiate=true agentResponse=404 text/markdown`; awesome-blog public/data/recipe-library.md tracked (git ls-files); pwa-build.mjs:12 lists it in the precache set

area: process-html.mjs: heading ids (duplicates created, no uniqueness)
current_behavior: globby('./dist/**/*.html'); JSDOM-parses each file; for every h2/h3/h4 WITHOUT an id (`if (heading.id) continue`) sets id = textContent.trim().replace(/[\s.,?:]+/g,'-').replace(/-+$/,'').toLowerCase(). Existing ids are respected (not overwritten). No de-duplication; keeps apostrophes/parens/other punctuation in ids; whitespace-only heading gets id="".
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: Overlay build of all 106 posts + recipes: duplicate ids on 27 pages with process-html vs 3 pages without it (e.g. the recipe article has `cooking-flow`, `ingredients`, `before-you-start` each x15 on one page; other posts have `web-dev`x2, `before`x2). Duplicate ids break in-page anchors (always jump to first) and fail HTML validity. Slug algorithm also differs from the blog's own heading-id/`.heading-link` logic, so existing #fragment links from posts/search engines can change.
proposed_resolution: Make heading ids part of the Markdown pipeline (blog renders its own ids/anchor links) and change process-html to either skip /blog and /recipes output or de-duplicate with -2/-3 suffixes and strip unsafe characters; add a built test asserting unique ids per page and that existing anchor targets in posts resolve. Keep fragment compatibility for links like #cooking-flow.

area: process-html.mjs: html-minifier-terser options and CSP safety
current_behavior:
minify(html, {removeComments:true, preserveLineBreaks:true, collapseWhitespace:true}). No minifyJS/minifyCSS/conservativeCollapse/ignoreCustomComments. Processes every dist/**/*.html (incl 404.html, 500.html). Inline <script>/<style> contents are not minified but leading indentation and trailing blank lines are trimmed (experiment: '
   import ...
   
' became '
import ...
'). <pre>, <textarea>, <code> inside pre keep whitespace; inline svg <text> whitespace is collapsed; <iframe>/<noscript>/<table> are preserved/normalized.
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: Safe for the real content: comparing raw astro output to processed output for all 145 overlay pages, text of 124 <pre>, 533 inline <script>, 169 <style> is byte-identical (0 diffs), so Astro's CSP hashes (computed before this pass) survive for scripts AND styles. Residual risk: an inline script/style Astro hashes that happens to start with whitespace would break its hash; built-csp.test.mjs checks scripts only, not <style> hashes (matters if style-src-elem hashes are adopted, see CSP entry).
proposed_resolution: Keep options for pre/script/style safety, add a style-hash assertion to built-csp.test.mjs. Fix the Svelte hydration regression below in the same commit.
evidence: cmp-pre.mjs result {pre:124,preDiff:0,script:533,scriptDiff:0,style:169,styleDiff:0}; style-hash-check: 169 style elements, 0 hash mismatches after processing (SRC-style CSP build); exp-minify.mjs output

area: process-html.mjs: strips Svelte SSR hydration markers and whitespace nodes (pre-existing bug, will hit every recipe/blog island)
current_behavior: Svelte 5 SSR output inside <astro-island> contains comment anchors (<!--[-->, <!--]-->, <!---->, <!--[-1-->) and inter-element whitespace text nodes that hydrate() relies on. removeComments:true deletes all markers; collapseWhitespace:true deletes whitespace-only text nodes between elements. Raw dist/index.html has 10+ marker comments; the processed one has 0 comments.
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: Today the SiteNavigation island on every page already hydrates by discarding and re-rendering its DOM (MutationObserver in Playwright: 2 island elements removed on load with process-html, 0 without). Blog/recipe islands (PostCards, Search, Navigation, RecipePage, RecipeLibrary, dialogs) would be torn down and rebuilt on load: layout shift, lost SSR benefit, focus/scroll loss. Preserving only the comments is NOT enough: the minifier removing the whitespace text node still causes `hydration_mismatch` (reproduced).
proposed_resolution: VERIFIED fix: add `conservativeCollapse: true` and `ignoreCustomComments: [/^\[/u, /^\]/u, /^$/u]` to the minify options. Applied to a copy of the blog-merged raw astro output (145 pages): `node --test scripts/built-csp.test.mjs` passes (1 test, 145 pages), style-hash-check = 169 style elements / 0 mismatches, 124 <pre> + 533 inline scripts + 169 styles byte-identical to raw, nav island removed-element count 0 on /all-posts/ and /about/ (2 with the current options), no console warnings; index.html grows ~123 B. Independent of the merge: this can ship as its own small PR against current main ahead of the merge (the SiteNavigation island is affected in production today); add a Playwright check that island DOM nodes survive hydration. Also consider skipping process-html's heading-id pass for blog content (see duplicate-id entry).
evidence: hyd.mjs/hyd2.mjs in scratch: minified {removedElementsInIsland:2}, raw {0}, comments-only fix {2 + console warning https://svelte.dev/e/hydration_mismatch}, conservativeCollapse+ignoreCustomComments {0, no warnings}. Overlay recipes pages show noisy counts (dynamic islands mutate legitimately), so the nav island is the clean signal; per-island verification still required in implementation; patched-options verification: built-csp.test.mjs pass on patched output (145 pages), style-hash-check styleHashMismatch 0, cmp-pre preDiff/scriptDiff/styleDiff 0, hyd2.mjs patched removedElementsInIslands 0 vs 2 for original processing

area: built-csp.test.mjs: what it asserts and gaps for blog/recipes
current_behavior: Reads vercel.json header Content-Security-Policy; asserts it exists, does NOT match /(?:^|;)\s*(?:script-src(?:-elem)?|default-src)\s/ and DOES contain frame-ancestors 'none'. Then for every dist/**/*.html: requires <meta http-equiv=content-security-policy> in <head>, policy matches default-src 'self', has a script-src directive without 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval', and every inline <script> (module/js, non-empty text) has its sha256 in script-src and the meta precedes the script.
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: It already iterates all pages, so blog/recipe pages are covered automatically for inline scripts: overlay build (145 pages incl 106 posts + 31 recipe pages) PASSES under both DST CSP and the blog's CSP. Gaps it will NOT catch: (a) intersection of meta + header policies (img-src https images, frame-src embeds) -- real blocking found in browser tests; (b) style-src-elem hashes if the blog's split style policy is adopted; (c) service-worker registration scope/worker-src; (d) form-action; (e) external hosts used in built HTML that no directive allows.
proposed_resolution: Extend with: 1) compute, per page, every external subresource host (img/srcset/iframe/source/link/script) and assert it is allowed by BOTH the meta policy and the Vercel header policy using CSP fallback rules (img-src->default-src, frame-src->child-src->default-src); 2) assert inline <style> hashes appear in style-src-elem when present; 3) assert the header and Astro meta do not both define img-src/frame-src (single source of truth); 4) keep existing script assertions; 5) add a Playwright smoke over representative pages (post with CloudFront images, YouTube/nbviewer/diagrams.net embeds, recipes page with SW) that fails on any securitypolicyviolation event.
evidence: built-csp.test.mjs passed in overlay (`npm run build` tail: pass 1 fail 0, 145 pages); csp-check.mjs Playwright runs below

area: CSP intersection: vercel.json header vs Astro meta policy blocks blog content
current_behavior: Header: `img-src 'self' data:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests`. Astro meta (built): `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' <hashes>; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`. A resource must satisfy both policies. No frame-src, connect-src, worker-src, manifest-src, form-action set (they fall back to default-src 'self' in the meta).
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: Reproduced in Chromium with the overlay build served with the vercel.json header: (1) every https://d1d7p8ufhgz4ld.cloudfront.net image (the only external image host in built blog pages: 627 references; 129 console violations across 8 sampled pages; 105 broken images on /all-posts/ alone) is blocked by header img-src AND meta default-src; (2) YouTube (13 iframes), nbviewer.org (2) and viewer.diagrams.net (1) iframes are blocked by meta default-src fallback ('Framing ... violates default-src'). Same-origin images, recipe SW registration (scope /, active) and scripts are fine. With the blog's directive set in astro.config AND the header img-src widened to https: (or the CloudFront host), 0 violations and 0 broken images on all 8 sampled pages incl. SW.
proposed_resolution: Single source of truth: move img-src/frame-src/connect-src/form-action into astro security.csp.directives (blog's list: img-src 'self' https: data:, frame-src youtube/youtube-nocookie/viewer.diagrams.net/nbviewer.org) and remove img-src/style-src from the vercel.json header (keep frame-ancestors, object-src, base-uri, upgrade-insecure-requests, which meta cannot express or is redundant). Prefer pinning img-src to https://d1d7p8ufhgz4ld.cloudfront.net instead of bare https: if no other host appears (only host seen in 145 built pages). Decide whether to rehost images (removes the dependency on the blog's CloudFront/S3 stack, which is also being retired with the AWS infra).
evidence: csp-check.mjs (Playwright) outputs: DST CSP+header -> `Loading the image 'https://d1d7...cloudfront.net/...' violates ... img-src 'self' data:` and `Framing 'https://www.youtube.com/' violates ... default-src 'self'`; SRC CSP + unchanged header -> 129 img violations, frames allowed; SRC CSP + header img-src https: -> 0 violations, sw active; external hosts in built pages: cloudfront x627, youtube x13, nbviewer x2, diagrams x1 (cdnjs/jsdelivr/unpkg occurrences are escaped code samples, not loaded resources)

area: CSP: style policy split (blog) vs unsafe-inline (DST) and inline styles
current_behavior: DST allows `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` in both meta and header. Blog uses styleDirective resources [{self, kind:element},{unsafe-inline, kind:attribute}] which emits `style-src-elem 'self' <sha256 hashes>; style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'` (verified in overlay build).
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: 61 built pages (posts) contain style="" attributes, so attribute-level unsafe-inline must stay for blog content (50 post sources have style=). Adopting the blog's stricter element policy is feasible: 169 style elements, 0 hash mismatches after process-html. But CSP is global per build (security.csp in astro.config), so jsolly pages are also moved to the stricter policy; and header `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` still permits inline elements at the header layer (policies intersect, so the meta stays authoritative).
proposed_resolution: Adopt the blog's split policy globally (stricter, passes), delete the duplicate style-src from vercel.json, and add the style-hash assertion to built-csp.test.mjs. Keep style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline' because post HTML uses style attributes (or sanitise them at build via the blog's sanitize-html step).
evidence: overlay build meta: `style-src 'self' ; style-src-elem 'self' 'sha256-..' x4; style-src-attr 'unsafe-inline'`; dom-audit: styleAttrPages=61; style-hash-check.mjs: {pages:145, styleElements:169, styleHashMismatch:0} on both processed and raw dist

area: Recipe PWA: service worker scope '/' collides with the whole jsolly.com origin; hook ordering; legacy installs
dst_file_lines: (new code) awesome-blog scripts/recipes/pwa-build.mjs:6,53-86, src/components/recipes/recipe-pwa-client.mjs:13, public/recipes-pwa/manifest.webmanifest; DST process-html.mjs (runs after astro build); DST public/favicons/site.webmanifest; Layout.astro:79
current_behavior: Blog registers /recipe-service-worker.js with scope '/', precaches ~hundreds of URLs (recipe route, /favicon.ico, /data/recipe-library.{json,md}, /media/recipes/*, /recipes-pwa/*, every JS/CSS/font referenced by the recipe pages), and answers navigations for the hard-coded route /post/15-minute-dump-and-go-instant-pot-recipes/ from cache. A second worker is written next to the old recipe route as a legacy scope. Manifest id/start_url/scope: '/post/15-minute-dump-and-go-instant-pot-recipes/' and '/'. The integration runs on astro:build:done (before process-html.mjs).
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: (1) Registered on jsolly.com the worker controls the entire origin (scope '/') and caches /favicon.ico etc. (confirmed: registration active with scope http://127.0.0.1/ in browser test); a bug or stale snapshot could affect jsolly.com pages. (2) DST already ships a different manifest (/favicons/site.webmanifest, Layout.astro:79); the recipe manifest is only linked on recipe pages. (3) The worker cache key hash is computed from pre-process-html bytes, so changing process-html output does not bump the cache version (stale snapshots). (4) DST production smoke blocks service workers (production-smoke.mjs:89 serviceWorkers:'block'), so the SW is never exercised in prod. (5) For users who installed the PWA on blogthedata.com, the old worker (scope '/') keeps answering /post/15-minute... navigations from cache and its update fetch of /recipe-service-worker.js will hit a redirect, which service worker update checks refuse -- they would never see the 301 to jsolly.com/recipes (needs a non-redirecting self-unregistering worker at both old SW URLs on blogthedata.com; also /.well-known is reserved and cannot be redirected on Vercel).
proposed_resolution: Re-scope: serve the worker from /recipes/ (e.g. /recipes/service-worker.js with scope /recipes/), update manifest id/start_url/scope to /recipes/, adjust ROUTE and the precache URL list; move the PWA build step after process-html (or into a postbuild script) so the cache hash covers final bytes; add an Accept/matcher exemption for the worker script; add a Service-Worker-Allowed or Cache-Control: no-cache header rule (blog has it for the legacy file); ship a kill-switch worker (unregister + clients.navigate to https://www.jsolly.com/recipes/) at /recipe-service-worker.js and /post/15-minute-dump-and-go-instant-pot-recipes/service-worker.js on the blogthedata.com project so installed PWAs migrate. localStorage key 'blogthedata-recipes-v2' is origin-scoped and will not carry over (document the loss or add a one-time migration prompt).
evidence: pwa-build.mjs:53-81 (worker source), :85-87 (astro:build:done hook), recipe-pwa-client.mjs:13 register('/recipe-service-worker.js',{scope:'/'}); browser test: `/recipes/meals/ sw: http://127.0.0.1:4421/ active`; awesome-blog vercel.json:80-88 header for the legacy worker; vercel.com/docs/routing/redirects/configuration-redirects ('/.well-known ... cannot be redirected or rewritten'); production-smoke.mjs:89

area: vercel.json: headers, redirects, trailingSlash, status codes, limits
current_behavior: trailingSlash true; git.deploymentEnabled main only; one redirect: host jsolly.com -> https://www.jsolly.com/:path* with permanent:true; one global header block (nosniff, Referrer-Policy, X-Frame-Options DENY, the CSP above). Live apex redirect returns HTTP 308 (Vercel maps permanent:true to 308).
what_breaks_or_conflicts_when_blog_and_r: (1) John asked for per-path 301s: `permanent:true` yields 308 on Vercel; 301 needs `statusCode: 301` explicitly. (2) vercel.json allows max 2,048 redirects (docs); fine for ~107 posts + categories but any wildcard catch-all must be last. (3) The blog's vercel.json header rules (Content-Type for /rss,/rss/,/atom,/atom/, no-store for /release.json, no-cache for the SW) have no equivalent in DST and must be re-pathed to /blog/rss etc. (4) /.well-known cannot be redirected, so blogthedata.com/.well-known/security.txt must remain a served file on whichever project owns blogthedata.com. (5) Blog's vercel.json sets framework/buildCommand/outputDirectory; DST relies on auto-detect (keep DST's).
proposed_resolution: Keep the redirect rules for blogthedata.com in the blogthedata project's own vercel.json (not in jsolly's file) with statusCode 301 per path, host-scoped `has` rules; port only the Content-Type/Cache-Control header rules to DST under /blog/*. Do not add blog hosts to this project's redirect array.
evidence: live curl https://jsolly.com/about/ -> HTTP/2 308; vercel.com/docs/routing/redirects/configuration-redirects (Number of redirects 2,048; permanent 308/307); awesome-blog vercel.json:35-88

area: astro.config.ts merge
current_behavior: DST: site by NODE_ENV (localhost:4321 dev else https://www.jsolly.com), integrations svelte()+sitemap({customPages: resume PDF}), CSP default-src 'self' + style unsafe-inline, tailwind vite plugin. No markdown config, trailingSlash default 'ignore', no PWA integration. Blog: static, trailingSlash 'always', prerenderConflictBehavior 'error', recipePwa integration, markdown {syntaxHighlight:'prism', processor: satteri({smartPunctuation:false, gfm:false})}, strict CSP list, server host 127.0.0.1.
